newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Strikers man roadblocks in Argentine provinces.
newsitem.headline: Strikers man roadblocks in Argentine provinces.

text.p: Protestors cut off major highways throughout Argentina Thursday, as the 24-hour general strike called by opposition unions hit the nation's provinces much harder than the capital Buenos Aires.
Demonstrators cut access roads to two of Argentina's largest cities, Rosario and Csrdoba, where local media reported many businesses closed and an absence of public transport.
Roadblocks isolated the capital of the northwestern province of Jujuy, San Salvador, and in the far south cut the road between the Patagonian provinces of Neuquin and Rmo Negro.
In Buenos Aires, the government said bus services were only a fifth normal levels. But the subway was working normally and train companies put on extra services to cope with added demand.
With bus services cut to a trickle, traffic jams clogged access roads into central Buenos Aires. But after arriving downtown, workers piled into offices, shops and cafes as usual.
